problem: If $\overset{―}{A}={\sqrt{2},\sqrt{7},\sqrt{13}}$ and $\overset{―}{B}={\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5},\sqrt{7},\sqrt{11}},$ then what is $\overset{―}{A\cap B}?$
worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for intersections states that

$$
\overset{―}{A\cap B}≡\overset{―}{A}\cup \overset{―}{B}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A\cap B} & =\overset{―}{A}\cup \overset{―}{B} \\  & ={\sqrt{2},\sqrt{7},\sqrt{13}}\cup {\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5},\sqrt{7},\sqrt{11}} \\  & ={\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5},\sqrt{7},\sqrt{11},\sqrt{13}}.\end{aligned}
$$
